messages:
marta: Heads up — saw a p95/p99 latency blip on a subset of hosts since last night's model push. Not the usual kernel flip pattern.
aj: saw it too. Alerted by perf-bot ~03:10 UTC. p99 went from ~180ms -> ~720ms on ~12% of GPU nodes for short requests (<=64 tokens).
ben: any rollout id or model version pinned? I can correlate with deploy logs.
marta: model: redwood-open-3.2b @ v2026-03-16-22:12 (tokenizer update + reduced vocab merge). Rollout was canary across hosts tagged region=us-west-2:batch-small
sophia: initial hypothesis: tokenizer change shifted subtokenization -> more short sequences with many small subtokens causing prefetcher misprediction? saw KV cache hit drop ~12% on affected hosts.
luca: that would explain more KV churn and different seq-len distribution. But why kernel routing would spike latency? Prefetcher -> kernel-decider path picks a different kernel if estimated latency > threshold.
perf-bot: metric snapshot 03:05-03:20 UTC: affected hosts (n=43): p50 40ms->45ms, p95 180ms->410ms, p99 180ms->720ms, throughput -7%. KV-hit 0.78->0.68
aj: I grabbed a flamegraph from one host (attached): heavy time in prefetcher.poll_and_route() and kernel_selection.evaluate_fastpath().
ben: can you paste the small repro of inputs that hit the slow path? we can run local profiler.
marta: here's a short example that reproduced it locally:
```
input: "Can you summarize the latest billing changes?"
model settings: seq_max=256, early_stop=false, batch_hint=adaptive
```
sophia: running that locally with v3.2b+tokenizer yields kernel_decider choosing kernel_v2_quant for first tokens then flipping to kernel_v1_generic after KV-miss pattern.
luca: kernel_v1_generic has worse per-token latency for short sequences due to smaller cooperative warps. The kernel_decider uses prefix-length heuristics + prefetch score. If prefetcher underestimates upcoming KV use, it picks v2_quant, then realizes misses and flips — that flip is expensive (recompile-ish warm path + syncing).
aj: we saw recompile spikes in host logs: "kernel hotflip: trigger=route_mismatch, compile_time=230ms" on affected hosts.
ben: ok actionable: 1) rollback tokenizer change on canary and stop rollout, 2) add a temporary conservative prefetch threshold to avoid fastpath flips, 3) add metric to trace kernel_flip_count per-request.
marta: initiated rollback via deploy-bot: @deploy-bot rollback canary redwood-open-3.2b:v2026-03-16-22:12
deploy-bot: rollback started for canary group region=us-west-2:batch-small — estimated completion 03:48 UTC :gear:
aj: added conservative flag to runtime config on those hosts: `kernel_decider.prefetch_margin=0.2` (was 0.05). Pushing now.
sophia: can we patch kernel_decider to avoid immediate hotflip within same request? maybe only allow flip after N tokens or when seq_len_estimate diff > threshold.
luca: good idea. I'll open a tiny PR to gate flips for short-request class and add telemetry.
marta: current status: rollback in progress, config patched on affected hosts, perf-bot shows p99 trending down to ~220ms on sample hosts after config change.
perf-bot: new snapshot 03:55 UTC: affected hosts p99 720ms->230ms, KV-hit back to 0.76, kernel_flip_rate dropped 85%.
ben: follow-ups: run A/B on a small stable canary with tokenizer change + conservative prefetch to see if we can keep tokenizer benefits without perf regression.
aj: I'll schedule an eval run with synthetic seq-length hist matching production. Also add end-to-end perf test to our rollout checklist for tokenizer changes.
marta: filing a postmortem ticket with root-cause: tokenizer subtoken distribution shift -> increased KV churn -> prefetch underestimation -> kernel_decider hotflip -> latency spikes. Action items listed. Thanks y'all :thumbsup:
